newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia c.bank leaves December rates unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Croatia c.bank leaves December rates unchanged.

text.p: The National Bank of Croatia will leave its monetary policy unchanged and plans no rate cuts in December to help banks, it said in a press release on Thursday.
It mentioned no lowering of the reserve requirement, now at 35.85 percent of total kuna deposits. It was last cut by 1.1 points in October.
The central bank's discount rate has been steady at 6.5 percent since a cut from 8.5 percent in August. The benchmark Lombard rate has been unchanged at 11 percent since September.
At a meeting late on Wednesday its board decided that the banking sector liquidity was relatively high and the kuna exchange rate also remained stable, requiring no major operations.
"The usual seasonal increase in demand for cash and its (deteriorating) effects on the banks' liquidity will be covered by temporary purchases of hard currency," it said.
It stayed out of the foreign exchange market last month.

The bank said it would also provide banks in need for kuna funds with Lombard loans. It planned to further decrease loans to the central government, but mentioned no details. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
